title: Jeden dzień · wszystko
note: Capstone situation_chunk unit — the final A2 unit. ZERO new material: every phrase is copied verbatim (same string, same diacritics) from one of the five live Situations units — a2_shopping_func, a2_directions_func, a2_ordering_func, a2_phone_func, a2_smalltalk — all of which sit before this node on path_order (indices 63, 69, 83, 89, 54; this node is 99). teaches_lemmas is empty: nothing is taught here, only recombined. The point of the unit is SITUATION DISCRIMINATION, not recall — each of the five source units already tests recall of its own phrases in isolation; this one mixes them so Dad has to pick the phrase that fits the scene he's actually in, not just the phrase he remembers. HOMOGRAPH CHECK: because every item is a whole previously-taught chunk-string and no item clips, re-inflects, or partially reuses a taught form, the homograph trap (a form taught as one thing being reused as another) cannot arise here — there is no new surface form anywhere in the file to mis-tag. Verified each of the ~45 recycled phrases against the owning unit's own teaches_lemmas/match list before use; none altered. DELIBERATE DISCRIMINATION TRAPS built into quiz: Nie wiem. (street) / Nie słyszę. (phone) / Nic nowego. (small talk) look alike at a glance and are tested against each other directly (Q9). Wszystko w porządku. (small talk answer to Co słychać?) vs To wszystko, dziękuję. (shop/restaurant till close) share the word wszystko but do opposite jobs (Q11). To zły numer. (phone) vs To daleko. / To blisko. (street) share the To ___ shape (Q10). Four Czy...? openers from four different situations are set against each other in Q12. STRUCTURE: focus/teaches_structures carry situation_chunk, following the convention already set by all five source units (each re-declares teaches_structures: [situation_chunk] even though the id was first taught earlier — this file follows the same house pattern). uses_structures is the union of everything the five source units used. Title check: 'Jeden dzień · wszystko' uses only jeden / dzień / wszystko, all exact-taught pool lemmas — no untaught Polish form in the title, per the AGENTS title rule. Intro slide titles were held to the same bar and built only from taught chunks/words (przyimki-style builder jargon like powtórka was deliberately avoided, even though it appears in older A1 review-unit titles, because it is not in POOL).

intro.title: One day, nothing new
intro.body:
This is the last unit of A2, and it teaches you no new Polish at all. Every phrase in it you already own — from the shop, the street, the restaurant, the phone, and small talk.

What's new is the mix. Up to now each situation was practised on its own. Here they're shuffled together, the way a real day actually goes: you buy something, you ask the way, you eat somewhere, your phone rings. The skill being tested is not "can you remember the phrase" — it's "can you tell which phrase belongs to which moment."
intro.body_pl: Sklep. Ulica. Restauracja. Telefon. Co słychać?

intro.title: Czy…? Nie…? To…? — three shapes, five situations
intro.body:
A handful of openings repeat across every situation, and that is exactly where mix-ups happen. Czy…? starts a question in a shop, on the phone, and in the street — the shape is identical, the job is not. Nie…? and Nic…? sit right next to each other and mean three completely different things depending on where you are. To…? does the same.

None of this is new grammar — you are not learning a rule here. You are learning to look past the opening word to what actually follows it, because that is what tells you the situation.
intro.body_pl: Czy jest chleb? Czy mogę rozmawiać z mamą? Czy to daleko?

intro.title: How to end each scene
intro.body:
Every situation has its own way of closing, and they are not interchangeable. A shop or restaurant visit ends with To wszystko, dziękuję. A phone call ends with Do usłyszenia — never with a goodbye built for standing in front of someone. Directions in the street end with Dziękuję bardzo.

One trap: Smacznego! looks like it belongs at the end of a meal because it is said around food, but it is said TO you, before anyone eats. It opens the meal, it does not close it — Było bardzo smaczne. is what closes it, afterwards.
intro.body_pl: To wszystko, dziękuję. Do usłyszenia. Dziękuję bardzo.

rows: said TO you, before eating — not a close

intro.title: A whole day, four stops
intro.body: Here is the whole thing chained together — shop, street, restaurant, phone — in the order a real day might actually run. Nothing in it is new; every sentence is a chunk from one of the five units you already finished. Read it once as a story before you start the exercises.
intro.body_pl: Poproszę chleb. To wszystko, dziękuję. Przepraszam, którędy do centrum? Czy jest wolny stolik? Poproszę zupę. Słucham? Nie mogę teraz rozmawiać.

examples.en: At the shop: A coffee, please.
On the street: Which way to the bank?
At the restaurant: Is there a free table?

quiz.prompt: You walk into a shop and want a coffee. You say:
quiz.explain: Poproszę + the thing you want is the shop-and-café frame. Rachunek is what you ask for at the end of a meal, not at a shop counter.

quiz.prompt: You're lost and need to ask a stranger which way to the chemist's. You say:
quiz.explain: Którędy do…? is the street question — no verb, just do plus the genitive place you already know.

quiz.prompt: You've just sat down at a restaurant and want to see what they have. You say:
quiz.explain: Paragon is the shop till receipt — a different piece of paper entirely from the restaurant menu.

quiz.prompt: Your phone rings. You pick it up and say:
quiz.explain: Słucham? is the phone pickup. The other three all belong to a restaurant, the street, or a shop.

quiz.prompt: A friend asks how your weekend was, and it was great. You say:
quiz.explain: The other three all close something — a shop visit, a phone call, a set of directions. Było super answers Jak było?

quiz.prompt: You've finished shopping and you're at the till. You say:
quiz.explain: Smacznego is said to you before a meal, not by you at a till. Do usłyszenia closes a phone call, not a shop visit.

quiz.prompt: You want to know if you can talk to your brother on the phone. You say:
quiz.explain: All four start with Czy, but only rozmawiać z bratem asks for a person on the phone.

quiz.prompt: Your food has just arrived. Before anyone starts eating, the waiter says one word to you. He says:
quiz.explain: Smacznego is said the moment food arrives — nothing to do with a phone line or small talk.

quiz.prompt: Someone stops you in the street and asks the way. You have no idea. You say:
quiz.explain: All three look alike at a glance. Nie słyszę is for a bad phone line, Nic nowego answers Co słychać?, and only Nie wiem answers a stranger's question in the street.

quiz.prompt: A stranger has dialled your number by mistake. You tell them:
quiz.explain: To daleko is a street phrase about distance, not a phone phrase about a wrong number — the To ___ shape is shared, the situation is not.

quiz.prompt: A friend greets you in the street and asks how things are. You say:
quiz.explain: Both contain wszystko, but To wszystko, dziękuję closes a shop or restaurant visit — it does not answer Co słychać?

quiz.prompt: You're standing beside an empty table in a restaurant, checking if it's free. You say:
quiz.explain: All four start with Czy, but each belongs to a different place — shop, street, phone, or here, a restaurant table.
